docs.title: limbdark
docs.text:
Gaussian priors for limb darkening coefficients from Claret & Bloemen (2011) and Claret (2017).

Uses Monte Carlo interpolation to propagate uncertainties in stellar parameters (Teff, logg, [Fe/H]) to uncertainties in limb darkening coefficients for Bayesian transit analysis.

docs.title: Python
docs.text:
import limbdark as ld

u1, u1_err, u2, u2_err = ld.claret(
    band='Kp',
    teff=4970, uteff=120,
    logg=4.25, ulogg=0.03,
    feh=0.0, ufeh=0.2
)

docs.title: How it works
docs.text: For a given photometric band and limb darkening law, limbdark interpolates the Claret tables on a 3D grid of (Teff, logg, [Fe/H]) to obtain limb darkening coefficients. Uncertainties are propagated by drawing Monte Carlo samples from the stellar parameter distributions and interpolating each sample on the grid. The resulting distributions of limb darkening coefficients can be summarized as Gaussian priors for use in transit fitting.

docs.title: Supported laws
docs.text: Law Coefficients Formula linear u I(μ) = 1 − u(1 − μ) quadratic u1, u2 I(μ) = 1 − u1(1 − μ) − u2(1 − μ)² squareroot u1, u2 I(μ) = 1 − u1(1 − μ) − u2(1 − √μ) logarithmic u1, u2 I(μ) = 1 − u1(1 − μ) − u2 μ ln(μ) nonlinear u1, u2, u3, u4 I(μ) = 1 − Σ uₖ(1 − μ^(k/2))

docs.title: Python API
docs.text:
The main function is limbdark.claret():

import limbdark as ld

# Quadratic limb darkening (default)
u1, u1_err, u2, u2_err = ld.claret(
    band='Kp',
    teff=5800, uteff=100,
    logg=4.44, ulogg=0.05,
    feh=0.0, ufeh=0.1
)

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Description band Photometric band (see Reference) teff, uteff Effective temperature and uncertainty [K] logg, ulogg Surface gravity and uncertainty [cgs] feh, ufeh Metallicity and uncertainty [dex] n Number of Monte Carlo samples (default: 100000) law Limb darkening law (default: 'quadratic') kind Interpolation method: 'nearest' (default) or 'linear' transform Transform quadratic (u1, u2) to Kipping (q1, q2) space (default: False)

docs.title: Return values
docs.text:
Depends on the law:

  • linear: u, u_err
  • quadratic/squareroot/logarithmic: u1, u1_err, u2, u2_err
  • nonlinear: u1, u1_err, u2, u2_err, u3, u3_err, u4, u4_err

docs.title: Kipping transform
docs.text:
For quadratic law, the Kipping (2013) reparameterization ensures uniform sampling in physically allowed parameter space:

q1, q1_err, q2, q2_err = ld.claret(
    band='Kp', teff=5800, uteff=100,
    logg=4.44, ulogg=0.05,
    feh=0.0, ufeh=0.1,
    transform=True
)

docs.title: Command line
docs.text:
limbdark --teff 5800,100 --logg 4.44,0.05 --feh 0,0.1 --band Kp

Options:

  • --law — limb darkening law (default: quadratic)
  • -n — number of MC samples (default: 10000)
  • -t / --transform — use Kipping transform
